clue.text: How accelerating motorist was masterful

parts.note: a driver speeding up presses hard on the pedal, and the same phrase is the idiom for asserting authority firmly

explanation.surface: A description of a driver forcefully speeding away.
explanation.walkthrough: The motoring picture is literal: pressing the accelerator. The idiom for taking a firm stand is the same phrase, so 'was masterful' is the real sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means insisting firmly on something and refusing to yield, which is behaving in a commanding way.

clue.text: Censor lady cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of the name is lopped off

parts.note: Edith is a woman's name, standing for any lady

explanation.surface: A woman with her hair or speech trimmed by a censor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut short' removes the final H from EDITH.
explanation.definitionFit: To censor a text is to remove or alter parts of it, which is what an editor does in cutting it.

clue.text: Firm hold on travelling bag

explanation.surface: Someone clutching a holdall tightly.
explanation.walkthrough: A grip is also an old word for a holdall or small travelling bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm hold is a clasp or grasp; a travelling bag of this name is a holdall, a chiefly British usage.

clue.text: Checking bleeding pencil

parts.note: a stick of alum used by men to stop shaving cuts from bleeding is named with this adjective before pencil

explanation.surface: A pencil that has been bled on, or one that stops blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Checking' means stopping, not inspecting, and the pencil is a shaving stick of alum rubbed on nicks to staunch them.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a substance that contracts blood vessels and so stops bleeding, as in the shaving stick.

clue.text: Lean person after Sunday travelling round leaving lake

indicators.note: after means what follows comes behind the Sunday letter
round says the remaining letters are turned about into a new order
leaving means the lake letter departs from the word travelling

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A thin traveller setting off on a Sunday, skirting a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaving' drops one of the two Ls, and 'round' shuffles what is left; 'after' puts that behind the S. A starveling was once a common word for a half-starved person or animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A starveling is an undernourished, emaciated creature, a thin figure.

clue.text: I am introducing stuff of no real importance

indicators.note: introducing means the first piece comes in front of the next

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
stuff as a noun means material, the substance of something

explanation.surface: Someone presenting something trivial.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe of I'M is ignored, as usual in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Something immaterial is irrelevant and does not matter.

clue.text: Sign here, it is no exaggeration

explanation.surface: An official form asking for a signature, insisting it is accurate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign here' is read as where you sign: under the statement on a form.
explanation.definitionFit: A signature goes beneath a written declaration; and saying less than the truth is the opposite of overstating.

clue.text: Be numb when unwell

definitions.meaning: adjective here, standing for the phrase meaning to be off colour

explanation.surface: Advice that illness leaves you numb.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, failing to sense your own body is being numb; as an idiom it means being a little ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbness is a lack of physical sensation in your body; the idiom means being slightly off colour.

clue.text: Government document that's anything but colourful

explanation.surface: A dull official report.
explanation.walkthrough: A white paper is a British government policy document setting out proposals before legislation.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a policy report is issued by ministers; and blank white sheets are as uncolourful as it gets.

clue.text: Priest, the Parisian turned up and I followed

indicators.note: turned up in a down answer means the word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: le is the French word for the, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A Parisian cleric arriving, followed by the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' reverses the French article, as the answer is a down entry; 'followed' says the I comes after it. Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Eli was the biblical priest at Shiloh who brought up the boy Samuel.

clue.text: Gold to complete car

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A gold finish completing a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complete' simply says the word 'to' rounds off the symbol for gold; it is not a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Auto is a chiefly American short form of automobile, a motor vehicle.

clue.text: Not in favour of returning gratitude for tank

parts.note: V stands for versus, meaning against

indicators.note: returning means the gratitude word is read backwards

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: An ungrateful person against giving thanks for a tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' makes AT from TA. TA is everyday British slang for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A vat is a large container for liquids, as used in brewing or dyeing.

clue.text: New cost ie right more than once for desk

indicators.note: new says the letters are formed into a fresh arrangement
more than once means the letters before it are used twice

explanation.surface: A new desk costing, that is, quite right several times over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More than once' doubles IER (IE plus R for right) to IERIER; with COST these ten letters are rearranged by 'New'.
explanation.definitionFit: An escritoire is a writing desk with drawers and a hinged writing surface.

clue.text: Another day with trailer or something found under it perhaps

indicators.note: another suggests a different version of the letters, a reworking

explanation.surface: Another day spent with a trailer, and what lies beneath it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' is the anagram signal; 'it' points back to the trailer, beneath which the tyres sit, so the definition leans on the wordplay's own word.
explanation.definitionFit: A radial-ply tyre is fitted to wheels, so it is found beneath a trailer.

clue.text: Final scoot round using system of notation

indicators.note: round signals the letters are moved about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone riding a scooter round a last time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' is the anagram signal, not a lap on the scooter. Tonic sol-fa writes music with syllables doh, ray, me and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic sol-fa is a method of writing and teaching music using syllable names for notes of the scale.

clue.text: Vessel that has been taken out of the water

indicators.note: taken out of means the letters of that are removed from the phrase the water

explanation.surface: A container lifted out of the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T, H, A, T in order from THE WATER, leaving E, W, E, R.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug or pitcher, a vessel for water.

clue.text: Overlook study that has been completed

parts.note: to con is to study or learn carefully
completed means done, finished

explanation.surface: Someone ignoring a piece of research once it is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: To condone wrongdoing is to accept or forgive it, letting it pass unpunished.

clue.text: Evident that it can be seen

explanation.surface: Something plain because it is in view.
explanation.definitionFit: Visible means plain and obvious, and also capable of being perceived by the eye.

clue.text: Left aircraftsman to take quarter of milk-sugar

parts.note: AC is the RAF abbreviation for aircraftman
SE, south-east, is one of the compass quarters

explanation.surface: An airman taking a quarter-pint of milk.
explanation.walkthrough: LAC is also the RAF abbreviation for Leading Aircraftman, which disguises the split L + AC.
explanation.definitionFit: Lactose is the sugar found naturally in milk.

clue.text: Has to assemble part of colonnade

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Workers obliged to put up a section of columns.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across haS TO Assemble.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a classical Greek covered walkway lined with columns, a portico.

clue.text: Possibly silver fish used as surreptitious substitute

parts.note: silver coins are an example of loose change
ling is a long cod-like sea fish

explanation.surface: A silvery fish being slipped in as a secret replacement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silver' means coins here, not the metal colour of a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore a changeling is a fairy child secretly left in place of a stolen human baby.

clue.text: Very long time in the one-sided match

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A lopsided match that seems to last forever.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across thE ONe-sided.
explanation.definitionFit: An eon is an immensely long period, an age.

clue.text: Diminutive man, not son, having time at school

indicators.note: not says the son word is removed from the word before it

parts.note: a lesson is a period of teaching at school
taken as written

explanation.surface: A small man without his boy, spending time at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diminutive' means a shortened name, not a small person: Les is short for Leslie.
explanation.definitionFit: Les is the pet form of the name Leslie, a short name for a man.

clue.text: All in France look out for custom

explanation.surface: A French phrase and a trader seeking business.
explanation.walkthrough: Tout is French for all; to tout is to solicit customers.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for everything; and a street seller tries to attract buyers by pestering passers-by.

clue.text: Not in the country his substitute who's bizarre

parts.note: not in means out, away from home
a country is a land

indicators.note: substitute suggests the letters of his are swapped about

explanation.surface: An absent stand-in for someone abroad who is odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Substitute' rearranges HIS into ISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Outlandish means strange and unfamiliar, wildly unconventional.

clue.text: A big hit up on the line

indicators.note: up in a down answer means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a six is the biggest single hit in cricket, clearing the boundary

explanation.surface: A huge cricket shot landing on the boundary line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' turns SIX into XIS under A. A six in cricket is a hit over the boundary rope without bouncing.
explanation.definitionFit: An axis is an imaginary straight line about which something rotates or is symmetrical.

clue.text: Do not admit from Delaware and new York

parts.note: DE is the postal abbreviation for Delaware
Y stands for York, as in YMCA-style abbreviations

explanation.surface: Someone from Delaware and New York refusing entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New York' is split: new gives N, York gives Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny a claim is to refuse to accept or confess it.

clue.text: One is not paid for such conduct

definitions.text: One is not paid for such conduct

parts.words: One is not paid for such conduct
parts.note: an amateur receives no pay, and behaviour falling below the standards of a trade is described the same way

explanation.surface: Someone working unpaid on account of their poor behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as bad conduct, but literally it describes being an unpaid amateur.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not paid is an amateur, not a pro; behaviour breaching workplace standards is described by the same adjective.
